# What it is
parametersD provides an object storing a set of parameters, that can be updated both during runtime, as well as during simuation execution through command line arguments or serialized interfaces e.g. xml.

# Usage

## Basic Usage
A new parametersD object automatically has access to a set of predefined [parameters](02_parameters.qmd), which are often used. These predefined parameters can be found in [parameters.h](https://gitlab.com/openlb/release/-/blob/3dedbdd2c4d5e911eda3784643dd419b211951d0/src/case/parameters.h).
Setting up new parameters is done by defining them in the olb::descriptors namespace in global scope of the case
```cpp
namespace olb::parameters {
	struct PARAMETER_NAME_1 : public descriptors::FIELD_BASE<1> { };
	struct PARAMETER_NAME_2 : public descriptors::TYPED_FIELD_BASE<bool, 1> { };
}
```
Multiple types of parameters are available for different data types and even allow definition of initial values

To set the parameters, first create the parametersD object and then set values for the parameters.
```cpp
MyCase::ParametersD myCaseParameters;
{
	using namespace olb::parameters;
	myCaseParameters.set<PARAMETER_NAME_1>(0.0078125);
	myCaseParameters.set<PARAMETER_NAME_2>(     true);
}
```
As the [[|Case Object]] is created with this initial parametersD, they can always be retrieved from the case like this
```cpp
auto& parameters = myCase.getParameters();
```
Retriving individual values of the parameters is done like this
```cpp
const T    param1 = myCaseParameters.get<parameters::PARAMETER_NAME_1>();
const bool param2 = myCaseParameters.get<parameters::PARAMETER_NAME_2>();
```

## Advanced Usage
Specific functors or models provide their own parametersD, to hold necessary information. Interacting with them works the same way.
This prototype for an Poiseuille inflow profile functor shows this
```cpp

struct PoiseuilleF {
	struct CENTER : public descriptors::FIELD_BASE<0,1> { };
	struct NORMAL : public descriptors::FIELD_BASE<0,1> { };
	struct RADIUS : public descriptors::FIELD_BASE<1,0> { };
	struct U_BULK : public descriptors::FIELD_BASE<1,0> { };

	using parameters = meta::list<CENTER,NORMAL,RADIUS,U_BULK>;
	using result_t = descriptors::VELOCITY;

	template <typename V, typename PARAMETERS>
	Vector<V,2> compute(Vector<V,2> physR, PARAMETERS& parameters) any_platform {
		const auto n = parameters.template get<NORMAL>();
		const auto center = parameters.template get<CENTER>();
		const auto r = parameters.template get<RADIUS>();
		const auto maxU = 3./2.*parameters.template get<U_BULK>();

		return ...;
	}
};

int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
	
}

```

## Serialize and Deseralize
Parameters can be deserialized from the command line interface or other serial formats like xml. 
Calling
```cpp
myCaseParameters.fromCLI(argc, argv);
```
reads the parameters from the command line interface during runtime. 
Overwriting parameters is done like this
```bash
./app --PARAMETER_NAME_1 1.2345 --PARAMETER_NAME_2 false
```
To list all available parameters run
```bash
./app --help
```


# Implementation Details
parametersD stores a map from parameter name to its value and is build on the legacy [cliReader](https://gitlab.com/openlb/release/-/blob/3dedbdd2c4d5e911eda3784643dd419b211951d0/src/io/cliReader.h).
